text: Something in you gets seen as lovelier than you know yourself to be. Your Neptune sits on their Venus, which puts the least defended part of you directly on the part of them that decides what is worth loving. The effect starts with them. They find something about you beautiful in a way they cannot fully explain, and if you ask what exactly they mean, the answer comes back in weather and music rather than in traits. That is flattering, and it is also a little beside the point, because much of what they are describing came out of their own longing and found you standing conveniently nearby. From your chair the pleasure is quieter and just as real. Their taste gives your imagining a place to land. Whatever you have been reaching for without a name, they can point at something in the room that holds a piece of it: a song, a color, the way a table is set, a face. You spend a good deal of your life slightly short of the object. Around them the object turns up. Two things follow, and both are worth watching without alarm. The first is that their standards go soft near you. Venus keeps a running price on things, and the function you bring does not deal in prices at all. They may forgive in you what they would forgive in nobody else, and feel rather good about doing it. Neither of you arranged that. You will usually be the last to notice, because from inside your own weather there is no weather. The second is the pose. Being someone's picture is comfortable for exactly as long as you can hold still, and you cannot hold still. When the ordinary version of you turns up, tired and specific and out of patience, what comes back is a confusion neither of you has words for. They feel let down by something you never promised. You feel accused of a failure you cannot locate. It helps to be dull on purpose early: let them meet your bad habits and your unglamorous opinions while the picture is still setting. There is a question of scale sitting under this. Neptune holds one stretch of sky for about fourteen years, so if the two of you are near in age, what their taste has fastened onto is something a whole band of births carries and you were the one standing in front of them. A generation between you makes it particular. The contact itself will not tell you which case you are in. What the contact can hand you, once the picture has been corrected a few times, is the experience of being liked with your outline on. That is rarer than being adored, and it wears differently.

A softer standard is on offer to them, and they are free to leave it on the shelf. Your Neptune makes a workable angle to their Venus. What you carry that has no edges sits within reach of the part of them that decides what it likes, and neither function is under any pressure from the other. When it does get used, the sign is usually taste. You show them something you would not show most people, and it goes in without being assessed first. They come back to it later, having thought about it. Their liking widens by a degree: less about what is smart to admire, more about what actually moves them. Few people can do that to them without it turning into a lecture, and you manage it because you are not arguing for anything. What comes back to you has practical shape. Your imagining tends to hover. Theirs is a function that can choose, arrange, and enjoy, so near them your formless enthusiasms turn into things you can actually have. A picture on a wall. An afternoon that happened rather than one you meant to have. Company on an evening you would otherwise have spent circling a mood. Kindness stays cheap and roughly even between you. Nobody is keeping a tally and nobody ends up short. The boundary trouble that shows up on tighter contacts of this kind does not arrive here by itself: their sense of what they will accept stays intact unless they decide to blur it, and nothing in you is pressing on it. Disuse is the real risk. A sextile supplies an opening and no engine. The two of you can stay warm, vague, and mostly out of touch for years, thinking well of each other and doing nothing about it, with no crisis to point out what is going unused. Somebody has to propose the actual plan, and given the two temperaments in play, waiting for it to be you is a slow bet. Taken up on purpose, this becomes the connection where being unclear is not a problem. You can bring something before it makes sense and have it treated well instead of solved.

They keep asking what things are worth, and you keep answering in a register with no numbers in it. Your Neptune squares their Venus, so what you idealize sits at an awkward angle to what they value. The trouble almost never arrives as a fight. It arrives as a matter that will not resolve. From their side you are hard to price. They want to know where they stand with you, what the arrangement is, whether the regard they are extending is being matched. Your answers are honest and they settle nothing, because fixed terms are not how your function holds a connection at all. A direct question about status can produce something warm, sincere, and completely unusable. They walk away with an impression instead of a fact, and impressions do not survive a week as well as facts do. From your side they can seem to be pricing what should not be priced. When they ask who is putting in more, or what the two of you are to each other, it can land on you as a small insult to the thing itself. It is not one. Their function is doing the only job it has, which is deciding what is worth what, and near you that job is genuinely difficult. Then there is the picture. Squares press, and this one presses your capacity to see a person as more than they are onto the part of them that enjoys being admired. It can run pleasantly for a long time. When the correction comes it arrives for both of you at once. They have been receiving a regard aimed slightly past them, and you have been fond of something you assembled. No one built that deliberately. Both of you are inside it before either notices. Watch the over-giving too, in whichever direction it runs. Vagueness invites effort, and when the terms are unclear one of you starts making up the difference with kindness. Kindness nobody asked for collects a debt that cannot be presented, since it was never agreed. The traction here is real and mostly yours to take. This person will keep asking the concrete question. Answering it once, in a sentence they could repeat to somebody else, costs you almost nothing and changes the texture of everything after it. None of the imagining is lost by putting one plain line underneath it. What you get in exchange is a person who stops guessing and starts telling you what they actually feel, which turns out to be more interesting than the version you were picturing.

Fondness moves between you without anything checking it at the border. Your Neptune trines their Venus, and the easy result is that the way you imagine and the way they enjoy fit together with no effort from either of you. Mood does most of the work between you. Time spent with this person has a quality that is hard to report afterward and needs no activity to justify it. Long silences are comfortable. Things you make or find or play for each other land well, and mean more coming from you than the same objects would from anyone else. They are unusually forgiving of the parts of you that do not add up, which is not a courtesy you get everywhere. Your side of the trade is a kind of enlargement of their pleasures. What they like becomes, in your company, attached to something bigger than liking. A meal is not only a meal. Their taste gets less anxious near you, less concerned with being right and more with what is actually good. In return, their function keeps you tied to things that can be touched. Your imagination has an appetite no object satisfies, and Venus is the part of a chart that knows how to be satisfied. Watching somebody do that well teaches you something you cannot get from thinking about it. Easy angles stop nobody, so both standard risks apply with no signal that they have begun. Generosity drifts past the point you meant it to end, and nothing marks the moment. The impression each of you carries of the other goes uncorrected for years, because a trine produces no event that forces a comparison. That comfort is pleasant and it is not the same as knowing somebody, though it can be mistaken for it over a long stretch. Where the contact earns its keep is in bad weather. When something goes wrong for either of you, this is the one that shows up without needing the story explained first, and stays without turning the visit into an account of what happened. Nothing about that is dramatic. Across enough years it becomes the part of this that neither of you has to arrange.

You are reaching for something with no edges, and they are looking straight at you. Your Neptune stands opposite their Venus, which sets your capacity to imagine across from their capacity to be charmed, and the two get aimed at each other rather than out at the world. Oppositions give a long clear view, and the view is odd from both chairs. They can see you more distinctly than you see yourself, and part of what they see is furniture from their own wanting. You can often tell what would delight them before they say it, which is a real skill and leaves an honest question open: are you meeting a person, or completing a scene. This can run warm for a long time. When trouble comes it is small and factual. You are late, or ordinary, or short with somebody in front of them. They ask a plain question about what happens next and you have no plain answer to give. The reaction is out of scale with the event, because what broke was not the evening. It was an arrangement nobody agreed to out loud, in which you were going to be slightly more than a person and they were going to be enchanted about it. Expecting that moment serves you better than trying to prevent it. Two things were running at once, the imagining and the actual liking, and only one of them is fragile. The completion on offer goes both directions and is worth stating plainly. They know how to say what they want and be pleased when they get it. You know how to see past what a thing costs, and to care about something that has not proved itself. A person who only prices things ends up with a tidy, small life. A person who only imagines ends up holding nothing. Across this axis each of you gets a long look at the missing half in the least abstract form available.

Whatever they come at you with arrives somewhere soft, and that changes what they do next. Your Neptune sits on their Mars, so the least solid part of you occupies the same ground as the part of them that wants, pushes, and picks fights. Start with what works. Their drive is one of the few forces that can reach into your fog and come back out carrying something. You picture, they move. Near them your vaguer intentions acquire dates and outcomes, which is a service most people will never do for you. Their action changes too: it becomes less about winning and more about making. Some of the gentlest and most imaginative work of their life happens around you, and they may not credit you for it, since nothing you did looked like effort. The difficulty is what happens to their anger. It has nowhere to land. You do not counter, you absorb, and the argument they walked in with disperses into atmosphere. That is maddening from their end, and the maddening part is not that you are hiding. It is that there is genuinely nothing solid to meet. They can leave a disagreement feeling coarse and loud and somehow in the wrong, having said nothing they would take back. You did not engineer that. This is the angle doing what angles do. Watch what the contact does to your own directness. Standing next to somebody who wants things so clearly, it is easy to conclude that you do not really want anything. You do. It simply comes in a form that does not announce itself, and if you never state it you will get their agenda by default and mistake the quiet for agreement. Their picture of you is worth knowing about as well. A temperament that direct tends to read softness as either saintly or as a tactic, with not much room between. Both readings will pass over you at different times and neither one is you. The useful piece costs you the most: be specific. Give one plain answer when they ask for one, including a no. Let them see you annoyed about something trivial. A person who can locate you does not have to keep pushing to find out where you are.

What you picture turns out to be portable, because they are willing to go and do it. Your Neptune sextiles their Mars, an available link between your sense of what could be and their appetite for getting on with things. None of it is compulsory. Left alone the angle stays a friendly hum and nothing comes of it. Put to work, it looks like this: you supply the reason and they supply the legs. You are unusually good at telling this person what a piece of effort is for, and a destination is exactly what their function tends to run short of. People with a strong drive rarely lack energy. They lack something worth spending it on, and you can hand that over in a sentence without even meaning to. Running the other way, their willingness to begin rescues your ideas from the shelf. You know the pattern where a thing stays lovely and unstarted for a year, then two. They are the interruption to it. Beginning costs them almost nothing, and once a thing exists it can be argued with and fixed, which is more than it was doing inside your head. Their bluntness does not injure you the way that kind of bluntness often does. You can take a flat sentence from them as information rather than as an attack, so the two of you skip most of the elaborate softening other people need. That is worth using while you have it, and it is not a courtesy either of you had to negotiate. There is a smaller service running underneath all of this. Their appetite for a fight, kept at this comfortable distance, gives you a rough sense of where your own edges are. You are not being pushed. You are watching somebody push, close enough to learn the mechanics from, and people who go through life without an outline usually pick one up by borrowing. The likely failure is that nothing happens at all. No fight, no drift, no signal: just an angle nobody ever touched. Sextiles do not complain about being ignored, and this one can sit unused for a decade while the two of you stay on perfectly good terms. It wakes up on tasks. Bring them something you cannot finish alone, say plainly what it is for, and let them run at it.

Pressure comes at you and you give way without agreeing, which solves nothing for either of you. Your Neptune squares their Mars: the part of you with no fixed outline set against the part of them that wants a clear answer and wants it now. You will notice this first as tiredness. Their directness is not meant to injure you and it lands hard anyway. Asked what you want, you find the honest answer is complicated, that the complicated version invites impatience, and that the cheap way out is to go along and quietly not do it. That route is expensive. It costs them a real answer, and it costs you the habit of having one. They run into a different problem. Effort spent near you loses definition. They start something with force and find the shape of it shifting while they work, or discover that the thing they were fighting for was never quite what you meant. Some people simply feel less capable around a hard contact of this kind, less certain that wanting things plainly is respectable. If that turns up in them, it did not come from anything you said. There is a version of this where their frustration gets loud and reaches you as something far worse than the subject deserved, and a version where your softness reads as refusal and their next approach comes in harder. Those are the same misfire running in opposite directions. Nobody is working an angle on anybody. The signal degrades on the way across, and volume does not repair it. What they want from you may also be aimed slightly to the side of you: an idea of how you would be to have in their corner. And you may be picturing them as the force that will finally carry you somewhere, which is a great deal to ask of a person who is only strong. The work belongs mostly to you here, because their function is not built to wait. Answer the question that was asked, in the words it was asked in. Say no where the answer is no. Let the disagreement happen while it is still small, at the point where you first noticed you did not agree. Force that meets an actual position stops escalating, and this connection will teach you what your positions are, one uncomfortable sentence at a time.

What you dream up and what they do sit on the same current, and neither of you built the connection between them. Your Neptune trines their Mars, so their appetite for action runs through your sense of what would be worth doing without catching on anything. In practice they take you seriously in a way that action-first people usually do not take dreamers. A half-formed notion of yours gets treated as a plan in progress rather than as noise. They will start something on the strength of a feeling you described badly, and the strange part is how often it works out, because the feeling was pointing at something real. Their side of the trade is a quieting. Around you their competitiveness loses interest in itself. They want less to beat somebody and more to make something, and if their usual setting runs hot, that is a relief they may not be able to account for. Anything with care or craft at the middle of it goes well between the two of you: work that builds, mends, performs, or looks after people. An easy angle checks nothing, and that is the whole of the risk. Nobody is going to raise the practical question. Who does which part, what it costs, when it is due, what was actually agreed to on Tuesday: all of it can stay unexamined, because raising it would spoil a mood that is genuinely good. The mood is not the work, though. Two people can talk a project into feeling finished and have nothing to show for it a year on. Complaints are the other soft spot. Neither of you is inclined to raise a small grievance, you because you would rather not make an edge and they because they would rather act than discuss. Small grievances do not evaporate. They collect quietly and come out later at an angle nobody expects. A little deliberate hardness keeps this honest. Name a day. Ask the dull question in the middle of the good mood and watch the ease survive it. The current is not fragile. It only needs somebody willing to be boring inside it.

Across from you is somebody who has no trouble saying what they want, and that contrast does most of the work in this connection. Your Neptune opposes their Mars. Wanting in a straight line faces a function that would rather not draw lines at all. The parts get handed out early. You become the one who is too easily hurt, who never says plainly what would settle the matter, who somehow occupies the higher ground without having claimed it. They become the heavy: too loud, too pushy, the one who made a scene. Neither description holds up, and both are available at a moment's notice, which is why the two of you slip into them so quickly. What they meet in you is a surface that will not hold a punch. They arrive with a grievance and it passes through and comes out the far side unresolved, leaving them alone with the whole intensity of it. That feels like being made ridiculous. From where you stand, their approach registers as a demand you have no way to answer, and the harder they insist, the further your attention goes somewhere they cannot follow. Idealizing runs along this axis too, mostly from your end toward theirs. Their capacity to act can look like the thing you have always lacked: the one who will cut through, decide, and carry it. Admiration of that size is heavy to receive. It leaves them no room to be uncertain, and when they turn out to be uncertain you may feel let down by a promise nobody ever made. The trade is the point of the aspect, so it is worth being clear about. They know how to want something and go and get it. You know how to let a thing go, to be moved, to accept what cannot be fought. Each of you is short of exactly what the other has too much of, and standing across from a working example is slower than advice and far more convincing. Nothing elegant fixes this. Say the want out loud in one sentence and let them answer it. When their temper shows, ask what it is actually about rather than deciding from the tone. The distance across the axis does not close. What changes is whether the two of you keep casting each other in parts, or start describing what is really there.

Your imagining lands on the part of them that says yes to things. Your Neptune meets their Jupiter, and between the two of you there is very little that says no, or later, or how much. What you get is permission at a scale you would not extend to yourself. Ideas you normally keep back, because they cannot be defended, get picked up by this person and said out loud as though they were obviously worth having. Being believed in like that is a real event and not a common one. It is also a weight. Your idea comes back louder and more finished than it went out, and you can find yourself nodding along to a certainty you do not actually hold. What you do to them is quieter, and they will not see it happening. Their faith runs on having something to believe in, and you supply material with no bottom to it. A hunch of yours can be inflated indefinitely, since there is nothing firm inside it to stop the expansion. They end up committed to a version of a plan, or of the two of you, that nobody ever built. Their optimism did the building, out of what you gave it. Ordinary life is where this shows. Neither function counts well. Amounts, dates, and who agreed to what can drift for months with nobody noticing the drift, and the two of you will remember the same conversation differently while both reporting honestly. That is not a fault in either character. It is what happens when the only functions in the room are the one that enlarges and the one that dissolves. Some of what they are believing in may not be you at all. Neptune moves slowly enough that everyone born within a decade or so of you carries it in the same place, so a small gap in age means their faith is partly aimed at a whole era's worth of longing. A wide gap means it is aimed at you. The geometry keeps quiet about which; the difference in your ages is what tells you. What you can take from it is a bigger container for the things you sense and cannot argue for. This person will never ask you to prove any of it. That is the gift, and it works best when somebody else in your life still asks.

An idea you would have left vague can get a frame here, if you want one. Your Neptune sextiles their Jupiter, an optional link between what you imagine and what they are prepared to believe. The traffic that matters most runs outward from you. You bring something you cannot defend: a read on how a situation actually is, a feeling about a person, an intuition about what a piece of work wants to become. They take it, find the wider principle inside it, and hand it back in a form you could say to a stranger. Very little is lost in the handling, because their instinct is to enlarge rather than to correct. Going the other direction, you keep their beliefs from getting too tidy. They like a conclusion and they like it early. You are constitutionally unable to supply one, so near you their opinions acquire more room, more tolerance for the part of a question that stays open. They do not always thank you for it at the time. There is a mild generosity in the pairing that shows up in ordinary ways. They tend to give you the benefit of the doubt on the days you cannot explain yourself, and you tend to let their enthusiasms pass without the small correction most listeners cannot resist. Neither of you is doing anybody a favor. It is simply cheaper to be kind at this angle than at most. This is an offer and nothing more. Sextiles ask for nothing, and the two of you can enjoy each other for years without a word of it being put to use, with no signal that anything is going to waste. Nobody gets hurt by the neglect. The connection just stays smaller than it might have been, and there is no moment at which that becomes obvious. Used on purpose, this is where you find out whether the thing you have been sensing has a shape to it. Say it badly to them, deliberately, and listen to what comes back.

They want to say what a thing is, and you keep declining to be a thing that can be said. Your Neptune squares their Jupiter, setting your feel for what cannot be stated against their appetite for stating it, endorsing it, and making it larger. What they run into is a target that will not hold still. They summarize the two of you, or the plan, or what you meant, and the summary is confidently wrong in a way you cannot fully correct, because the accurate version is not a sentence. They read your silence as agreement. You read their summary as pressure. Both are reasonable readings and neither is right. What you do back is subtler. Their function is built to conclude, and around you conclusions stop arriving. Matters they had settled reopen. Beliefs they were fond of turn out to have gaps in them that you never pointed out, since you do not argue, you only fail to be convinced. A certain kind of confident person finds this unnerving and cannot say why. The hazard in the pair is inflation, and it should be named without alarm. Belief aimed at something with no outline can travel a long way from the evidence. They may end up expecting more from you than was ever offered, not because anybody oversold anything but because there was nothing in the offer to limit what could be read into it. You may end up leaning on their certainty as though it were a floor. Neither of you set that up on purpose. Squares grind, and both of you get something out of the grinding. You get the ability to say one true thing plainly when it matters, which your function will avoid for a lifetime if nothing ever asks. They get a faith that has learned to sit with not knowing, which is the only kind that survives contact with a hard year. The move that works is small. When they state your position for you and get it wrong, correct it once, out loud, in their register. It will feel crude to you. It is also the only version they can hear.

Belief comes toward you with no conditions attached to it. Your Neptune trines their Jupiter, so what you imagine and what they permit run together with almost nothing in the way. They make a good audience for the parts of you that do not survive cross-examination. The hunch you would not repeat at work, the thing you keep returning to without being able to say why, the sense that a situation is not what everyone insists it is: this person takes all of it seriously without needing it justified first. Most people cannot manage that, and being able to think out loud in front of somebody changes what you are able to think. In return you widen what they consider possible. Their sense of the world's size feeds on exactly the material you carry, and they come away from your conversations with more room in their head than they arrived with. Sympathy moves easily both ways. Forgiveness is quick here, sometimes quicker than the situation called for. The softness in an easy angle is that nobody in the pairing plays the doubter. Nothing you imagine strikes them as far-fetched, and nothing they believe strikes you as naive, so an enthusiasm can build between you for months on very little checking. The correction, when it comes, usually arrives from outside the two of you and feels rude when it does. Cost is the other blind spot, and this is an observation rather than an instruction. Neither of you counts well, and there is no friction in this contact to make either of you start. What the two of you take on together tends to be reckoned low: in money, in hours, and in what it takes out of a person. What you keep is a steadier relationship with your own imagining. Around this person it stops being something to apologize for or to translate before speaking. That confidence outlasts the connection, and it travels.

They are looking at you from the far end of a long axis, and what they see comes out larger than what is standing there. Your Neptune opposes their Jupiter: your talent for dissolving an outline against their talent for expanding one. Each of you can watch the other's move in detail while making your own without noticing. You get a clear view of their confidence at work. You can tell where the faith is genuine and where a large statement is standing in for something they have not looked at yet. You rarely say so. Pointing it out is not how your function operates, and the not saying is itself a move, one they can feel and cannot name. They see your reach in the other direction, into the parts of a matter that resist being settled. On a good day they find that valuable and want to make it public. On a bad day they find it evasive and want you to commit to a position. Both reactions come from the same instinct. The axis hardens when nobody notices it happening. They grow more definite each time you decline to be, and you grow more elusive each time they announce. Then the two of you are having a standing argument about clarity itself while the actual subject sits untouched on the table. Idealizing runs here in both directions, which is the part most worth watching. You may take their largeness as proof they know something you do not. They may take your depth for the meaning their life has been missing. Both flatter, both come apart eventually, and the coming apart feels like betrayal by someone who did nothing wrong. What completes across the axis is a pair of questions neither of you asks well alone. Theirs is what this means. Yours is what it actually is underneath the meaning. On a good stretch you keep their conclusions from arriving early, and they keep your sense of things from evaporating before anyone else gets to hear it.
